history.summary: 99-yr leasehold 1BR at Euhabitat, D14 (Eunos/Ubi), asking $780k at $1,343 PSF for an efficient 581 sqft. Huge 210-txn URA base is reliable, but the rate it certifies is a weak 2.66%/yr — and the unit is 1.08km from MRT.
history.rating_rationale: Data is trustworthy (210 txns) but tells an unexciting story: 2.66%/yr appreciation is below OCR baseline and well under inflation-adjusted targets. PSF ($1,343) sits below the $1,429 median but the slim discount plus poor MRT access (1.08km, 13-min walk) and lease decay cap upside. Low entry quantum is the main plus. A neutral hold — reliable but flat.
red_flags: 2.66%/yr appreciation is weak despite reliable 210-txn data

history.summary: Lowest quantum of the batch ($780k) in D14 Eunos with the deepest cohort data (37 cohort + 210 appreciation txns); asking $1,342 is modestly below the 1BR average, a credible if not dramatic value edge near the Paya Lebar growth corridor.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,342 psf ($780k, 581 sqft) is below the project's ~$1,425 psf 1BR average per EdgeProp, a modest ~6% discount. Critically, the honest cohort signal (psf_premium_vs_cohort -5.3% on a deep 37-txn cohort) is far smaller than the headline age-adj -29.6%, so I lead with the smaller, better-evidenced number - this is a fair-to-slightly-cheap entry, not a steal. Deep data (210 appreciation txns) removes quirk risk. D14 sits in the Paya Lebar Central/PLQ decentralised-CBD catchment, an OCR/RCR-edge location. Buy at medium: the value edge is real but modest and offset by documented build-quality gripes (poor noise insulation, blocks built close together).
red_flags: Resident reviews cite weak noise insulation and blocks built very close (privacy/ventilation)
